title: Write Lane 6: query surface must read accepted identity claims
evidence: PG-AUDIT-002 / PGRT-004 / PGRT-015. parallel-slam.md Prompt 6 (canonical) + dependency-ordered-superseded.md Prompt 5.

spec.description: Accepted identity claims are inert: the whole identity pipeline currently has no effect on what a caller sees. Lane 6 had a complete 10-item work order and never pushed.
spec.context: ROOT CAUSE: loaders/ask.py queries person rows directly and never reads identity_claim or merged_into, so accepted claims and merges do not change results. The resolver must expose accepted versus proposed claim state and ambiguity honestly, and missing capabilities must be explicit in output rather than silently degraded. Related silent-failure evidence: who() uses people.person_search MATCH which raises 'no such column', and the app catches ANY SQLite error and falls back to a LIKE scan, so the query LOOKS like it works. Specs survive in TWO independent places, both on branch agent/people-graph-audit-record-20260806 of sisodias/great-library-of-siso: research/people-graph-program-record/prompts/parallel-slam.md and research/people-graph-program-record/prompts/dependency-ordered-superseded.md. Cite both and reconcile any difference rather than silently picking one. Canonical lane numbering is parallel-slam; see .docs/lane-numbering-map.html in the Great Library, and note the off-by-one A(n)===B(n+1). MEASURED UPDATE: identity_claim holds ZERO rows (baseline §4.1), so wiring ask.py to read it is necessary but NOT sufficient - see TASK-0006. Also ask.py's FTS path silently falls back to a LIKE scan at 130x cost (§4.3) - see TASK-0011, a one-line fix in the same file.
acceptance_criteria: ask.py reads identity_claim and merged_into; accepted claims change results
Query tests prove WHICH execution path ran, not merely that a result returned
Missing capabilities are explicit in output
PGRT-004 and PGRT-015 convert XFAIL to PASS
